title: 2003 AMC 12A 18
statement: Let \(n\) be a \(5\)-digit number, and let \(q\) and \(r\) be the quotient and remainder, respectively, when \(n\) is divided by \(100.\) For how many values of \(n\) is \(q + r\) divisible by \(11?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(n=100q+r=(q+r)+99q\) and \(99\) is divisible by \(11,\) we have \(q+r\equiv n\pmod{11}.\)

So \((q+r)\) is a multiple of \(11\) exactly when \(n\) is a multiple of \(11.\)

Among the \(5\)-digit numbers, the count of multiples of \(11\) is \(\left\lfloor\dfrac{99999}{11}\right\rfloor\) \(-\left\lfloor\dfrac{9999}{11}\right\rfloor\) \(=9090-909=8181.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Since \(99\) is a multiple of \(11,\) \(q+r\equiv n\pmod{11}\)
